guide.description: diff <file1> <file2> compares two files line by line and reports what's different. A line printed with '< ' exists in file1 but not file2; a line printed with '> ' exists in file2 but not file1. Lines identical in both files print nothing — diff only shows what changed. The order of the two files matters: swap them and every < becomes > and vice versa.

examples.note: removed-from-old lines get <, added-in-new lines get >

exercises.title: A line only in the second file
exercises.task: Compare roster.csv and roster-v2.csv with diff. roster-v2.csv has one extra row at the end.
hints: diff <file1> <file2> — the file that HAS the extra row is file2

exercises.title: A line only in the first file
exercises.task: Compare roster.csv and roster-v3.csv with diff. roster-v3.csv is missing alan's row.
hints: The missing row belongs to file1, so it prints with <

exercises.title: Additions and removals together
exercises.task: Compare roster.csv and roster-v4.csv with diff. roster-v4.csv changed grace's role, dropped mia, and added leo.
hints: A changed row shows up as one < line (the old version) and one > line (the new version), since the text itself differs

criteria.label: Removed/changed lines with <, added/changed lines with >

exercises.title: Argument order flips the direction
exercises.task: Run the same comparison as before but with the arguments swapped: diff roster-v4.csv roster.csv. Notice every < and > flips compared to the last exercise.
hints: Same two files, reversed order: diff roster-v4.csv roster.csv
Whatever printed with < last time now prints with >, and vice versa

criteria.label: Direction is flipped from the previous exercise
